title: GCSE History: The 20th Century
intro: From the causes of the First World War to the Cold War and the US civil rights movement, how well do you know the twentieth century?

questions.prompt: Whose assassination in Sarajevo in June 1914 helped to trigger the First World War?
questions.explanation: Archduke Franz Ferdinand was heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary. His assassination set off a chain of alliances that led to war.

questions.prompt: Before the First World War, Britain, France and Russia were linked in which alliance?
questions.explanation: The Triple Entente grew from agreements made between 1904 and 1907 and faced the Triple Alliance.

questions.prompt: Which country joined Germany and Austria-Hungary in the Triple Alliance of 1882?
questions.explanation: Italy signed the Triple Alliance in 1882, although it entered the war against Germany in 1915.

questions.prompt: Which new type of battleship, launched by Britain in 1906, sped up the naval arms race with Germany?
questions.explanation: HMS Dreadnought was faster and more heavily armed than any earlier battleship, so Germany raced to build its own.

questions.prompt: What was the name of Germany's plan to defeat France quickly by advancing through Belgium?
questions.explanation: The Schlieffen Plan aimed to beat France fast, then turn to face Russia. Germany's march through Belgium brought Britain into the war.

questions.prompt: Which treaty, signed in 1919, set out the peace terms for Germany after the First World War?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, near Paris, in June 1919.

questions.prompt: Which article of the Treaty of Versailles is known as the 'war guilt clause'?
questions.explanation: Article 231 made Germany accept responsibility for the war, which was used to justify reparations.

questions.prompt: Which international organisation was set up after the First World War to help keep world peace?
questions.explanation: The League of Nations first met in 1920. The United Nations replaced it after the Second World War.

questions.prompt: Which country never joined the League of Nations, even though its own president had proposed the idea?
questions.explanation: President Woodrow Wilson championed the League, but the US Senate refused to approve joining it.

questions.prompt: In 1936, German troops marched into which area, breaking the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.explanation: The Rhineland was meant to stay demilitarised. Hitler sent troops in during March 1936 and Britain and France did not stop him.

questions.prompt: What name is given to the union of Germany and Austria in 1938?
questions.explanation: Anschluss means 'connection' or 'joining'. The Treaty of Versailles had banned it.

questions.prompt: The policy of giving in to some of Hitler's demands to avoid war in the 1930s is known as…
questions.explanation: Appeasement is most linked with British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain.

questions.prompt: Which 1938 agreement allowed Germany to take over the Sudetenland?
questions.explanation: Britain, France, Italy and Germany signed the Munich Agreement in September 1938 without Czechoslovakia at the table.

questions.prompt: Which 1947 US policy promised support to countries resisting the spread of communism?
questions.explanation: President Truman's speech set out the idea of containment, a key US policy in the Cold War.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the US programme of economic aid to rebuild Europe after the Second World War?
questions.explanation: The Marshall Plan gave billions of dollars to Western Europe, partly to make communism less attractive.

questions.prompt: In 1948 and 1949, the Western Allies flew supplies into West Berlin to beat a Soviet blockade. What was this called?
questions.explanation: For almost a year, aircraft carried food and fuel into West Berlin until the Soviet Union lifted the blockade.

questions.prompt: Which military alliance did the USA, Canada and several Western European countries form in 1949?
questions.explanation: NATO stands for the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Members agreed to defend one another.

questions.prompt: Which military alliance did the Soviet Union and its Eastern European allies form in 1955?
questions.explanation: The Warsaw Pact was the Soviet bloc's answer to NATO and lasted until 1991.

questions.prompt: In a 1946 speech, Winston Churchill said what had 'descended across the Continent' of Europe?
questions.explanation: Churchill's 'iron curtain' described the divide between the communist East and the democratic West.

questions.prompt: Whose refusal to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, sparked a famous boycott?
questions.explanation: Rosa Parks's arrest led to the Montgomery Bus Boycott, a major event in the US civil rights movement.

questions.prompt: Martin Luther King gave his 'I Have a Dream' speech during which 1963 event?
questions.explanation: About 250,000 people gathered in Washington DC for the march in August 1963.

questions.prompt: Which 1954 US Supreme Court case ruled that segregation in state schools was unconstitutional?
questions.explanation: Brown v. Board of Education overturned the idea of 'separate but equal' in public schools.

questions.prompt: Which 1964 US law banned discrimination in public places and in employment?
questions.explanation: President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act in July 1964.

questions.prompt: The United States entered the First World War in 1917.
questions.explanation: The USA declared war on Germany in April 1917, partly because of German submarine attacks on shipping.

questions.prompt: The Treaty of Versailles limited the German army to 100,000 soldiers.
questions.explanation: The treaty also banned conscription, tanks and an air force, and limited the German navy.

questions.prompt: The Soviet Union was a founding member of NATO.
questions.explanation: NATO was formed by Western countries partly to protect against the Soviet Union, which later led the Warsaw Pact.

questions.prompt: The Little Rock Nine were nine Black students who enrolled at a previously all-white high school in Arkansas in 1957.
questions.explanation: Federal troops were sent to protect the students so that they could attend Central High School.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explanation: East Germany built the Berlin Wall in August 1961 to stop people leaving for the West.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
questions.explanation: In October 1962 the USA and Soviet Union came close to nuclear war over Soviet missiles in Cuba.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Montgomery Bus Boycott begin?
questions.explanation: The boycott began in December 1955 and lasted over a year until buses in Montgomery were desegregated.
